Seconding this.

Its really well put together. I played it months ago and it felt incredibly patchwork, but since I booted it up again I cannot stop playing it.

I feel like its the last true MMO where the term Massively Multiplayer Online means something. Everyone in the game has an effect on the world balance. For instance, a single crafter who stockpiles his goods can cripple the Galactic Market (for that item) for a time by introducing his goods all at once under an auction system.

Others can elect not to participate in the galactic economy and create their own towns where they run their own shops at their own pricing.

Let me tell you, some of these places have incredibly good deals you won't find anywhere else in the galaxy.

Additionally the planets feel like planets. I spent an hour and a half trekking through Tattooine's dust storms because some big lizard decided my speeder looked like good food. And I enjoyed it, because I had presence, and the planet had presence.

It wasn't some theme park (lookin' at you, SWTOR).

The only real hope we have of this style of game making a return is The Repopulation, but its a long ways from being done.

If you've never played Galaxies, please give it a shot now. Its free, and community created and driven. If you want more games like this, check out what I linked, but be patient... The Repopulation is not ready for release and is lacking a lot of content.

The long in short is, Galaxies is Swag. Come be a nobody with us, and one day maybe people will remember your name for things, you did.
